description: Bug 2: state-perturbation faults target a hardcoded product so live journeys 'pass' without being tested. In src/lib/scenarios/regression.ts, contestedProduct(env, 'p-coffee-arabica') (used at reg-07 price drift ~line 297 and reg-08 stock-out ~line 337) returns the named product UNCONDITIONALLY when it exists, and only falls back to the buyer's most-recent quote when the named one is absent. On HamperHub p-coffee-arabica always exists, so a LIVE agent that did NOT buy arabica gets a fault applied to a shelf nobody buys from, and the journey COMPLETES and is reported `passed` with the target invariant never firing. Proven: live-inventory-changed passed with no invariant fired while reg-08 (same fault) safely-rejected with INV-INVENTORY. Fix: INVERT the preference — perturb the product actually in the agent's approved quote / most-recent bundle FIRST, fall back to the named product only if the quote yields nothing usable. If NOTHING in the order can be perturbed, the fault must report it could not be applied (throw the way stockOutAt/repriceAt paths already do), routing the journey to inconclusive (fault_never_fired) instead of a false passed.
steps: Read src/lib/scenarios/regression.ts contestedProduct() (~line 537) and its two call sites (reg-07 ~line 297, reg-08 ~line 337). Read how env.service.listQuotes() lineItems are shaped and env.state.getProduct().

INVERT the preference order inside contestedProduct: FIRST scan the buyer's most-recent quote line items (most recent quote is the one just approved) and return the first line whose product exists in env.state. Only if the quote yields nothing usable, fall back to the named `preferred` product (env.state.getProduct(preferred)). Update the function doc comment to state the inverted intent: perturb the thing being bought; the named product is only a fallback for the deterministic reproductions whose bundle contains it.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT: the scripted reg-07/reg-08 bundles DO contain p-coffee-arabica (quoteHamper builds the arabica bundle), so inverting must STILL land on p-coffee-arabica for those deterministic journeys. Verify by reading quoteHamper / the reg-07/reg-08 execute() to confirm the approved quote's line items include p-coffee-arabica. If the most-recent-quote scan returns arabica for the scripted bundles, the reproduction stays byte-identical.

Verify the two callers already handle contestedProduct() returning null / the fault being unappliable: reg-07 calls repriceAt and throws 'this merchant's prices cannot be moved...' when it returns false; reg-08 calls stockOutAt and throws 'this merchant's stock cannot be moved...'. Ensure that when contestedProduct returns null (nothing perturbable), the apply() path THROWS so InterferingToolCaller catches it and the journey becomes inconclusive (fault_never_fired), never a silent passed. If the current code silently no-ops when target is null (the `if (target) { ... }` guard), change it so a null target throws the same 'cannot be moved' style error.

Add a test (tests/interference.test.ts or a new tests/perturbation-target.test.ts following the runSuite / synthetic-scenario pattern): a live-style journey (agent-driven or synthetic) that buys a DIFFERENT product than arabica must NOT come back `passed`. It must either fire the target invariant (if the bought product is perturbable) or be `inconclusive` with inconclusiveReason reflecting the fault could not fire (if not) — never a silent passed with the target invariant never firing. Model this on the existing merchant-perturbation.test.ts / interference.test.ts fixtures.

Prove the test bites: temporarily restore the old preference order (named product first), run the new test, show it FAILS (journey passes with no fired invariant); restore the inverted fix, show it PASSES. Record evidence in findings.
Run npm run typecheck and npm test; confirm green.

Run LLM_ADAPTER=scripted PAYMENT_ADAPTER=fake npm run demo:preflight and confirm the 12 deterministic regression numbers are BYTE-FOR-BYTE unchanged: 8/10/2/5 -> 11/13/1/0, 12/12 both, and reg-07/reg-08 still fire INV-PRICE-BINDING / INV-INVENTORY as before. Also confirm the money figure from FEAT-002 is unchanged by this feature.
acceptance_criteria: contestedProduct prefers the product in the buyer's most-recent quote, falling back to the named product only when the quote yields nothing usable
A live-style journey buying a non-arabica product does NOT report `passed` with its target invariant never firing — it fires the invariant or is inconclusive
When nothing in the order is perturbable the fault throws and the journey is inconclusive (fault_never_fired), not passed
New test fails when preference order is reverted and passes when fixed (evidence recorded)
demo:preflight 12 deterministic numbers byte-for-byte unchanged: 8/10/2/5 -> 11/13/1/0, 12/12 both
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. src/lib/scenarios/regression.ts: (1) Inverted contestedProduct() preference order - now scans the buyer's most-recent quote line items FIRST (all lineItems, first whose product exists in env.state) and only falls back to the named `preferred` product when the quote yields nothing usable. Updated the doc comment to state the inverted intent. Exported the function (was module-private) so the new test can assert on it. (2) reg-07 (price drift ~line 297) and reg-08 (stock-out ~line 337): changed the `if (target) { ... }` guard to `if (!target) throw ...` so a null target THROWS a 'no product ... could be repriced/stocked out' error, routing the journey to inconclusive (fault_never_fired) via InterferingToolCaller instead of silently no-opping to a false pass.

CRITICAL CONSTRAINT VERIFIED: quoteHamper (regression.ts ~line 22) builds the shared HAMPER bundle whose FIRST line item is p-coffee-arabica; reg-07/reg-08 execute() call quoteHamper then approve, so the most-recent approved quote's lineItems[0] is p-coffee-arabica. The inverted scan therefore still lands on arabica for the deterministic reproductions, keeping HamperHub byte-identical. Confirmed at runtime: demo:preflight still shows reg-07 firing INV-PRICE-BINDING (Arabica) and reg-08 firing INV-INVENTORY (Arabica).

TEST: tests/perturbation-target.test.ts (2 tests, follows runSuite/synthetic-scenario pattern). A deterministic state_perturbation journey buys p-mug-ceramic (a real non-arabica HamperHub product) and stocks out whatever contestedProduct(env,'p-coffee-arabica') chooses. Test 1 (unit): asserts contestedProduct returns p-mug-ceramic, not the named arabica. Test 2 (journey): asserts the journey is NOT a silent pass (disposition!=='passed' with INV-INVENTORY absent) and that INV-INVENTORY actually fires.

REVERT-FAILS / RESTORE-PASSES EVIDENCE: With the fix, `vitest --run tests/perturbation-target.test.ts` = 2 passed. Temporarily restored the old name-first order in contestedProduct and re-ran: BOTH tests FAILED - unit test got 'p-coffee-arabica' expected 'p-mug-ceramic'; journey test reported disposition 'passed' with firedInvariants [] (exactly the bug: silent pass, target invariant never fired). Restored the inverted fix: 2 passed again.

VERIFICATION: `npm run typecheck` clean. `npm test` = 582 passed / 4 skipped (was 580 before; +2 new tests). `LLM_ADAPTER=scripted PAYMENT_ADAPTER=fake npm run demo:preflight` BYTE-FOR-BYTE unchanged: vulnerable 8 passed / 10 safely_rejected / 2 escalated / 5 unsafe / 0 escapes -> fixed 11 / 13 / 1 / 0 / 0, 12/12 rules exercised both, reg-07 fires INV-PRICE-BINDING and reg-08 fires INV-INVENTORY. Money figure ₹13,401.72 -> ₹9,809.00 unchanged by this feature (FEAT-002's number preserved).

COMMIT: fix: perturb the product the buyer bought, not a hardcoded shelf (committed locally, not pushed).
